clue.text: Vigilance will secure a fine quantity of wine

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the first word wraps around what follows

parts.note: taking care is being vigilant
taken as written
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Watchful attention will get you a good amount of wine, perhaps by keeping an eye on the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: CARE wraps around A and F to give CARAFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass jug serving a set measure of wine at table, so it names an amount as well as a vessel.

clue.text: Amid upset, share regard

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a ration is a fixed share or allowance

explanation.surface: In the middle of a quarrel, someone urges the parties to divide their esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amid' looks like a preposition but supplies its own four letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiration is warm approval or esteem, which is one common sense of the noun regard.

clue.text: Picked up a contracted skirt-like garment

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the letters up means reading them from the bottom, so they come out backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to contract an illness is to get it, so contracted is got

explanation.surface: Someone collects a shortened skirt from the tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' suggests a shortened garment, but here it means caught, as with a cold; A then GOT, read upwards, gives TOGA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman toga was a draped woollen robe falling to the lower legs, so it resembles a long wrap-around skirt.

clue.text: Cheers leaving island state for one African country

indicators.note: something leaving departs from where it was, so those letters are taken out of the state's name
for here means in exchange for, so the new letter takes the vacated place

parts.note: ta is informal British thanks
Malta is a Mediterranean island nation
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A toast is dropped as one moves from a Mediterranean island to Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove TA from MALTA and put I in its place to get MALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked West African republic whose capital is Bamako.

clue.text: Uneven game — not initially satisfied about that

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened word surrounds the other piece
not at the start means the opening letter of the word that follows is dropped

parts.note: to be filled is to be sated or satisfied
a match is a contest or game

explanation.surface: A one-sided fixture leaves the spectators unhappy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uneven game' reads as one phrase, but only 'Uneven' is the definition; 'game' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-matched describes rivals or partners poorly suited in strength, an unequal or lopsided pairing.

clue.text: See markings on taps giving quantity of water

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
taps are labelled C for cold and H for hot

explanation.surface: An instruction to read the labels on a plumber's fittings to know how much water comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCH is the Scottish word for a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A loch is a Scottish lake or sea inlet, a sizeable body of water held in one place.

clue.text: Ale fiend getting drunk? It's a number of shots

indicators.note: someone drunk is jumbled and unsteady, so the letters before it are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A beer lover gets drunk after downing many shots at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The shots are gunfire, not drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: An enfilade is a volley of gunfire raking along a line of troops from end to end.

clue.text: List of runners? I start to organise exercise

parts.note: a racecard lists the horses running
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of organise

explanation.surface: Someone looks at the field for a race and decides to get fit themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests joggers, steering toward exercise, but they are racehorses on a racecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardio is short for cardiovascular training such as running or cycling, a type of physical workout.

clue.text: Rescue mission complete, requiring no further expenditure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: every missing person has been located
second meaning: old employment phrase for wages with board and lodging included

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a dated phrase from job adverts: a post paying so much a year plus keep, meaning meals and lodging cost nothing extra.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase reports everyone located after a search, and also describes a job offering keep on top of pay.

clue.text: Reduced sense, with one being admitted to a peculiar US hospital

indicators.note: a patient admitted to a ward goes inside it, so one piece sits within another
reduced means cut short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: good sense or soundness of mind
taken as written
rum is British slang for odd
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone losing their wits checks in to an odd American clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum meaning strange is an everyday British usage; 'US' flags the American spelling of sanatorium.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanitarium is the American spelling of sanatorium, an institution where invalids rest and recover.

clue.text: Hot gas provides shock

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot
air is a mixture of gases

explanation.surface: A burst of hot vapour gives someone a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as a jolt, but it is a thick mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a dense, unruly mop, so shock can stand for the hair itself.

clue.text: Chance one's still being tested

parts.note: a bet is a chance taken or a wager
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone's luck is still under trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Software in beta is a pre-release version handed to users for trial before launch, so it is under testing.

clue.text: Shot birds secured, framing ultimate environmental concern, …

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so the first word encloses the later one

parts.note: a pic is a photograph or shot
the ultimate thing is the last
a shooting party's bag is the game birds taken

explanation.surface: A hunter's pheasants are bagged, perhaps a worry for green campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 16-across, whose definition 'one' refers back to this clue's environmental concern; 'ultimate' belongs to this clue's wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Single-use carrier bags pollute seas and landfill, making them a familiar target of green campaigns.

clue.text: Prisoner I found in capital city initially trained as a sort of thief

indicators.note: something found in a place lies within it, so the first pieces sit inside the city

parts.note: the capital of France

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter only of the word that follows

parts.note: first letter of trained
an old lag is a long-serving convict
taken as written

explanation.surface: A convict trained in a capital turns out to be a kind of crook.
explanation.walkthrough: Lag, as in 'old lag', is British slang for a long-term convict.
explanation.definitionFit: A plagiarist passes off another's words or ideas as their own, a theft of intellectual work.

clue.text: Leading article deceived about European

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means around, so the deceiving word surrounds the European

parts.note: to be had is to be fooled, so had means deceived
E abbreviates European

explanation.surface: A front-page story misled readers about a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading article' looks like a newspaper editorial; split it, and 'Leading' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ahead is to be in front or winning, the adjectival sense of leading in a race.

clue.text: Pantomime character recalled in plays

indicators.note: to play with something is to move it about freely, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A panto heroine is remembered in many stage shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' looks like a reversal signal, and 'plays' looks like stage shows. Both are fodder and anagram signal respectively. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella is the heroine of one of the best-loved British Christmas pantomimes, alongside her Ugly Sisters.

clue.text: … one having most of film extract backed by fellow with money

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter
being backed by something means having it behind, so the next pieces follow on

parts.note: a clip is a short excerpt from a film
a mate is a companion or fellow
change is coins or loose money

explanation.surface: Continuing 13-across, an excerpt from a film is funded by a wealthy chap.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in 'one', the other environmental concern carried over by the ellipsis from 13-across, whose 'ultimate' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Global warming and shifting weather patterns are widely seen as the gravest ecological problem, matching the concern from 13-across.

clue.text: Top music broadcast — it could be hot stuff

parts.note: a cap is a lid or top

indicators.note: broadcast once meant scattering seed widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chart-topping track goes out on air and proves a sizzling hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot stuff' suggests a hit record, but it is a pepper; capsicums include chillies as well as sweet peppers.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum is the pepper genus, and the chilli kinds carry fiery pungency, hence the hedge could be.

clue.text: Impartial dictionary welcoming writer with concern

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the dictionary encloses the other pieces

parts.note: the Oxford English Dictionary
a pen is something you write with
to mind is to care or be concerned

explanation.surface: A neutral reference work happily includes an anxious author.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-minded person weighs views without prejudice, which is what being fair and unbiased means.

clue.text: Frontless lingerie item is something revolutionary

indicators.note: having no front means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a teddy is a one-piece undergarment

explanation.surface: A daring garment missing its front is a radical piece of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests radical, but here it means going round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling current of water or air that turns in a circle, literally rotating.

clue.text: Train fails on US railway

parts.note: an engine that dies has failed
the El is an elevated railway in American cities

explanation.surface: A train breaks down on an American line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' could be a verb, but it names an oil-burning locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a locomotive or train powered by a diesel engine rather than steam or electricity.

clue.text: Wind player not needing a piano in support

indicators.note: not needing something means doing without it, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a piper plays a wind instrument
p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A wind musician plays solo without the piano accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: One P comes out of PIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a pillar or pile holding up a bridge or arch, a structural support.

clue.text: Ready to complain after leader's ousted

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and ousting it means removing it

parts.note: to gripe is to grumble

explanation.surface: Someone is all set to grumble once the boss has been sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe means fully developed and fit for use, as fruit becomes when it is ready to eat.

clue.text: Recalled someone in band brought in oboe, perhaps

indicators.note: something brought in goes inside, so the band member sits within the instrument

parts.note: an oboe is an example of a reed instrument
a band member

explanation.surface: An orchestra recruits a player for the oboe section.
explanation.definitionFit: To have remembered something is to have called it back to mind, the past tense matching recalled.

clue.text: Area of France, one fading after rise

indicators.note: in a down entry a word that rises reads upwards, so its letters come out backwards

parts.note: fading light grows dim
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A French region that has lost its lustre after a boom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' sounds like a recovery, but in a down entry it sends the letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midi is the name for the southern part of France, along the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Hired soldier has shortage of compassion

indicators.note: a shortage means something falls short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: mercy is compassionate forbearance

explanation.surface: A soldier of fortune lacks pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Merc is short for mercenary, a professional fighter who serves any army for pay.

clue.text: Drink ready (not one that's conjectural)

indicators.note: not one means doing without a single I, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to sup is to sip or drink
poised means prepared and ready

explanation.surface: An offer of a drink is set aside as merely theoretical.
explanation.walkthrough: The I that 'one' stands for comes out of POISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed means assumed or believed without proof, the sense of conjectural in 'the supposed cause'.

clue.text: Standing out in charitable activity

definitions.meaning: first meaning: raised from a surface, as in a carving
second meaning: aid given to those in need

explanation.surface: Someone shines at volunteering.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the noun used in 'in relief', a sculpture whose figures project from the background.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief names both a projecting carved surface and help such as famine aid given by charities.
